data.title: Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ following 24-hour outage: Here’s what that means - National | Globalnews.ca
data.summary: The Nov. 12-13 outage disrupted Exchange Online, its cloud-based email service, as well as Outlook, Teams, its Copilot AI assistant and other Microsoft 365 products. It affected governments in Canada, the U.S., Australia and Japan, as well as businesses, hospitals, trading firms and airlines. Microsoft cited a network strain in their outage, and said it was not related to artificial intelligence or a cyberattack. CEO Satya Nadella publicly apologized for the disruption. [...] Microsoft has issued a “Code Red” in order to “quickly implement lessons learned” following a 24-hour outage earlier this month, a spokesperson said. Microsoft said this work is its “top priority.” “Our customers and partners depend on our services, and we owe it to them to not only fix problems when they occur, but to do everything we can to keep them from happening again,” the spokesperson told Global News. [...] Privacy Policy. Kotak said outages are bound to occur, especially as we rely more and more on new technologies. Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform, told a Code Red review that the affected component had experienced “roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures,” according to a memo seen by Reuters.

data.title: Microsoft declares a code red in the middle of a 'Patchpocalypse'
data.summary: Microsoft declares a code red in the middle of a 'Patchpocalypse' Companies are racing to patch a record number of software flaws this year. Microsoft just found out how long its own fixes take to reach the world. Microsoft (MSFT) has declared a code red, its top-priority alarm, after a 24-hour outage this month, according to internal memos reported by Reuters. The goal is to fix future problems worldwide within an hour. A recent urgent fix took five to six days to reach everyone. [...] The Nov. 12-13 outage knocked out Outlook, Teams, and Copilot. The culprit was a flaw in Microsoft's own software, introduced in July, that went unnoticed for about four months. Microsoft ruled out hackers and AI agents. Microsoft promises business customers that Microsoft 365 will be up 99.9% of the time, which allows about 44 minutes of downtime a month. By Yahoo Finance calculations, one 24-hour outage used up nearly three years' worth, though not every customer was down that long. [...] Responders traded more than 11,000 messages across 11 Teams chats while the data they needed sat scattered across separate systems. The faulty component had "roughly ten years' worth of acceptable failures," Charles Lamanna, a Microsoft executive vice president, said in a code red review. The fix list includes dividing traffic by region, so trouble in one place doesn't spread everywhere, and also AI agents that comb through system data to find problems faster.

data.title: Microsoft explains tech failures that triggered global outage | The Seattle Times
data.summary: While the company’s report and statements were adamant that AI did not cause the disruption, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said last week that AI could cause similar outages, but not because of cyberattacks. While making the rounds at Microsoft’s Ignite conference, The New York Times’ DealBook Summit and in an interview with CNBC last week, Nadella said AI’s proficiency in catching bugs could cause major headaches in itself. [...] “This incident was confirmed not to be caused by a cyberattack, and we found no evidence of malicious activity,” the company said in its postmortem, released Friday. It added that “AI tooling” was also not to blame. But what hit Microsoft 365 — the company’s suite of products that includes Outlook, Teams and Copilot — on Nov. 12 preceded a wider storm of digital chaos, fueling uneasy feelings around cybersecurity. [...] A little more than a week after a global outage crashed a swath of Microsoft services, the company reiterated that the severe disruptions weren’t caused by a malicious actor or artificial intelligence. In its own final report on the incident, Microsoft firmly repeated that the outage was not due to anything other than a bug that lurked in the company’s servers since July.
